constraints.source_text: The Bachelor of Arts in History requires students to take 10 courses (40 units).
constraints.description: The major requires 10 courses totaling 40 units overall.
constraints.note: No single pool; this is the overall total composed of the other listed requirements.

constraints.source_text: All majors are required to complete HIST 201 Approaches to History.
Students can take up to three additional lower-division survey courses. However, if they prefer to take upper-division courses instead, they may.
constraints.description: Students may take up to three additional lower-division survey courses, or substitute upper-division courses instead.
constraints.note: The optionality to substitute upper-division courses instead is unusual but captured as part of the same rule.

constraints.source_text: The Department of History will accept scores of 4 or 5 on Advanced Placement European History, Advanced Placement United States History or Advanced Placement World History as a substitute for one course requirement at the lower-division level.
constraints.description: AP exam scores of 4 or 5 may substitute for one lower-division course requirement.

constraints.source_text: Six upper-division courses are required, of which at least two must be 400-levels.
Six upper-division courses are required, of which at least two must be 400-levels.
constraints.description: At least two of the six upper-division courses must be at the 400 level.

constraints.source_text: No more than 4 units of HIST 490x Directed Research may be counted as satisfying the upper-division seminar requirement.
constraints.description: No more than 4 units of HIST 490x may count toward the upper-division seminar requirement.

constraints.source_text: For geographic breadth, majors must take at least one course from four geographic areas. Those areas and the classes that fulfill them are listed below.
constraints.description: Majors must take at least one course from the Americas geographic area.

constraints.source_text: For geographic breadth, majors must take at least one course from four geographic areas. Those areas and the classes that fulfill them are listed below.
constraints.description: Majors must take at least one course from the Africa, Asia and the Middle East geographic area.

details.scope: Geographic Requirement: Africa, Asia and the Middle East

constraints.source_text: For geographic breadth, majors must take at least one course from four geographic areas. Those areas and the classes that fulfill them are listed below.
constraints.description: Majors must take at least one course from the Europe and the Mediterranean geographic area.

details.scope: Geographic Requirement: Europe and the Mediterranean

constraints.source_text: For geographic breadth, majors must take at least one course from four geographic areas. Those areas and the classes that fulfill them are listed below.
constraints.description: Majors must take at least one course from the Global or Transnational geographic area.

constraints.source_text: Majors must also take two class that focus on the period before 1800 and two that focus on the period after 1800 to show temporal breadth. The courses that cover those periods are listed below.
constraints.description: Majors must take two courses focusing on the period before 1800.

constraints.source_text: Majors must also take two class that focus on the period before 1800 and two that focus on the period after 1800 to show temporal breadth. The courses that cover those periods are listed below.
constraints.description: Majors must take two courses focusing on the period after 1800.

constraints.source_text: A single course may fulfill both a geographic and temporal requirement.
constraints.description: A single course may count toward both a geographic and a temporal breadth requirement.

constraints.source_text: All history majors must complete a capstone course in the fall and/or spring of their senior year (exceptions can be made for juniors who need to take it earlier). There are two ways to complete the history capstone: a History Honors Thesis or a History Capstone Exercise.
constraints.description: Students must complete a capstone requirement in their senior year via one of two tracks (Honors Thesis or Capstone Exercise).
constraints.note: Combines timing and choice of track; the Capstone Exercise is not a course and cannot be verified from a course list.

constraints.source_text: To apply for the Honors program, students need a 3.5 or higher GPA in all USC history coursework (although this can be waived in certain cases).
constraints.description: Entry into the History Honors Thesis track requires a 3.5 GPA in history coursework, waivable in certain cases.

constraints.source_text: They also need to take HIST 492 , both in the fall and spring semester. Those who take this track will be considered for honors in the major. Taking HIST 492 will count as their Capstone.
constraints.description: Honors track students must take HIST 492 in both fall and spring semesters as their capstone.

constraints.source_text: The History Capstone Exercise is a way for students to reflect upon what they have learned as a history major. They will need to fill out a google form (or submit their answers in essay form) where they will reflect upon the classes they took, the papers wrote, and the skills they have developed. They will also attend one of the “Capstone Conversation” events scheduled throughout the year, where they will discuss their answers and their experiences as a major in a larger group setting.
constraints.description: Students choosing the Capstone Exercise track must complete a reflective questionnaire/essay and attend a Capstone Conversation event.
constraints.note: This is a non-course procedural milestone; no procedure value in the taxonomy maps precisely, so DECLARATION_DEADLINE was used loosely.

unclassified.source_text: It is recommended that students complete HIST 201 early in their course of study.
unclassified.why: Advisory statement, not a binding requirement.
